feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: clear positioning, relevant progression, and solid platform/operations depth. Writing is polished and professional, but impact would improve with more quantified outcomes beyond scope metrics, and the structure has some redundancy and style inconsistencies.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior profile with a coherent career story: progression at NACo supports credibility and leadership readiness.  
- Strong domain relevance: digital strategy, Drupal/CMS modernization, analytics, multimedia, and advocacy communications are all well evidenced.  
- Generally high writing quality: concise, readable, and free of obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include measurable wins such as traffic growth, engagement lifts, email performance, cost savings, production efficiency, or adoption improvements.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly. Consolidating these sections would tighten structure and save space.  
- Fix style consistency issues: use serial commas consistently (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); standardize hyphenation (“organization-wide,” “member-facing,” “front-end” are good—apply consistently); and consider “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience.” Also, “Ranked among the top public universities…” adds little value and can be removed.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It reads clearly, but it’s slightly generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard CV phrasing.
- Lead with your current value proposition: senior digital strategy/communications leadership for mission-driven or advocacy-focused organizations.
- Add 1–2 concrete differentiators from recent roles, such as enterprise web modernization, editorial governance, or analytics-driven channel leadership.
- Tighten wording to reduce abstraction: replace “building the workflows and systems” with “designing scalable workflows, governance, and content operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “stakeholder coordination” are already echoed in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content” overlaps with advocacy/public-sector messaging elsewhere; keep it only if targeting policy-facing roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it sharper and less repetitive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, higher-impact phrasing: “Digital transformation strategy,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Web platform and CMS management,” “Editorial workflow and governance.”
- Replace vague items like “Multi-channel communication” with stronger, more senior wording such as “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Combine overlapping systems items: “Workflow & systems architecture” + “Editorial workflow design” could become “Content operations, workflow design, and governance.”
- Consider a tighter version: Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS management • Content operations & editorial governance • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Stakeholder & cross-functional leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several ideas already covered in the header and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, advocacy communication, analytics, and stakeholder coordination.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project section. Tighten it around 3–5 outcomes-led bullets and emphasize what is new since NACo.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client context: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate into sharper bullets, e.g.:
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved cross-channel content operations by redesigning workflows, governance, and analytics for web, email, social, and multimedia teams.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content requirements, and discovery UX.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/templates, publishing speed, stakeholder groups served, traffic, engagement, or efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats NACo and the summary; keep only what is distinct or newly scaled.
- Specific projects already appear in “Recent Projects,” so avoid re-describing them here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia operations, and budget oversight across website, email, social, and video.”
- Make bullets more outcome-led: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen measurable impact where possible: add newsletter list size, social growth/engagement, video output, reporting efficiency, or governance adoption/compliance improvements.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “including”/“along with” constructions with direct verbs; combine the email/social bullet into one concise line if metrics are limited.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; emphasize enterprise leadership, modernization, and systems here instead.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer projects; keep this entry focused on organizational capability built and business value.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, editorial operations, and channel growth during this period.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Tighten bullets and emphasize ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet around growth/launch impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing coordination and consistency.” Add metrics if available: open rates, production volume, turnaround time, stakeholder adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very close to the Director role’s opening.
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager entry and footer project.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive language:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications operations” if you want closer alignment with recent roles.
- If space allows elsewhere, add scale in experience bullets rather than here; skills sections should stay concise and non-generic.
- Keep wording parallel: all noun phrases, no mixed styles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one version consistently.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes over individual tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences**
- Drop lower-priority or older platforms here unless they are target-role keywords; keep **WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages** in Technical + IT instead.
- Remove **jQuery** from topline skills unless the role specifically asks for it; it dates the profile and adds little strategic value.
- If possible, tie this section more directly to recent impact by aligning wording with experience: **Drupal platform builds, modular microsites, structured content workflows, AI search**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the **Technical + IT** section almost line-for-line; use topline skills for themes, not full inventories.
- **CMS modernization**, **workflow automation**, and **AI-enabled search** already echo Core Competencies, so keep phrasing distinct and tighter.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool dump and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from software list to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” rather than just tools.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” instead of separate bullets if space is tight.
- Replace generic terms with stronger business language: “KPI framework development” and “executive reporting dashboards” instead of “KPI design” / “Leadership reporting.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive reporting dashboards • SEO, UX and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool list.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Core Competencies” and multiple NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and use sharper, more senior phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio buildout and operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems”
- Swap “Video production and editing” for “Broadcast-quality video production” to better reflect the studio-building leadership in the 2022–2024 role.
- Shorten “Hybrid and virtual event production” to “hybrid event delivery” unless virtual-only events are a major target requirement.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier elsewhere on the CV (not here), e.g., “built NACo’s first in-house studio” or “expanded in-house advocacy/event production capacity.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove one mention.
- “Studio operations” and “video production” are already evidenced in NACo roles, so this skills line should stay concise rather than repeat detail.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should emphasize depth/order and trim lower-signal tools.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling strength: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If formatting allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; modular campaign builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space is tight, drop **GitHub Pages** unless it supports a meaningful project; it reads less strategic than the rest.
- Keep this item platform-focused only; save implementation details for the coding/tools line.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**. Consider removing the platform names there or replacing that section with broader capabilities.
- Drupal already appears repeatedly in recent experience, so avoid overloading this line with extra Drupal wording unless you cut duplication elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and emphasize current, differentiating tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around execution depth, not basic languages: “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group modern tools by use case: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere.
- If accurate, add a qualifier tied to recent work: “used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, workflow automation, and lightweight serverless functions”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep one version shorter or make this one more specific.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” unless you want this section strictly implementation-oriented.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so tighten and frame around higher-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Remove lower-signal or dated tools unless central to target roles: **Basecamp, Trello**
- If space allows, add light functional framing instead of a pure list: **Airtable systems, no-code automation, project tracking, and team collaboration tools**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **Airtable** and **workflow automation** already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- **Slack** and **Teams** are common workplace tools; keep them only if you need keyword coverage, not as headline skills.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for the candidate’s communications leadership, but this item is too bare and misses the scale/complexity implied elsewhere in the CV. It should signal enterprise email/engagement capability, not just list brand names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, journey automation)**
- If accurate, add stronger qualifiers tied to recent work: **…audience segmentation • automated journeys • campaign deployment • member communications**
- Keep the list concise; only include platforms personally used in meaningful, recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience already showing email/newsletter leadership; avoid repeating outcomes here unless you add platform-specific depth.
- “Multi-channel communications” and newsletter scale are already covered elsewhere, so this section should emphasize systems/tools rather than responsibilities.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize foundational contributions that set up later leadership.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to stress early-career buildout and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence/reach of weekly videos, or team/process improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence around 2–3 core contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestream and video content, and provided day-to-day oversight for a digital media associate.”
- If accurate, swap vague phrases like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows” for measurable results or clearer actions such as launched, managed, produced, trained, or standardized.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or helping establish the format.
- “Strengthening workflows” and multi-channel support also appear in later NACo entries; keep this one focused on team formation and hands-on production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities, while contributing digital and multimedia content across organizational communications.”
- Make the podcast launch its own clause with stronger action verbs: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to digital content production” with specific outputs if known: web features, audio segments, interviews, campaign materials, or stakeholder-facing resources.
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes launched, audience growth, internal adoption, or programs/policy teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid overemphasizing broad digital/media leadership here; that is covered much more strongly in later NACo roles.
- “Multimedia production” repeats elsewhere—use “first podcast” and research/program support to keep this entry distinct.
